subject: FinLytics integration: post-call recap and 5xx repro/debugging
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@finlytics.com>, Joe Alvarez <joe.alvarez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: FinLytics integration: post-call recap and 5xx repro/debugging

Hi Sara / Joe —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap + action items so we have alignment on next steps: 

1) What we saw: your integration tests hit intermittent 5xx responses from our embed/reranker endpoint (~1-2% of requests during a ~10k request run). You shared that the calls are coming from a backend process that batches ~200 items per request.

2) Agreed investigation scope:
  - Redwood: help reproduce the 5xx, surface traces, and provide mitigation guidance (timeouts, batch sizing, token handling).
  - FinLytics: send a minimal reproducible payload, logs, and the timestamps of failing requests.

3) Short-term mitigations we suggested on the call: reduce embedding batch size to 32, increase client timeout to 60s for reranker calls, and enable streaming where possible.

Can you share the sample request JSON and one of the error logs from yesterday? That will let our engineers start reproducing locally. I’ve looped in Camila (integrations) and Neha (ML infra) — they’ll coordinate the repro.

Next meeting: let’s aim for Thurs 11/20 10:00 PT if that still works; tentative calendar invite sent.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@finlytics.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call recap and 5xx repro/debugging

Thanks Marissa — attaching a representative error log and a sanitized request payload. Keys removed for privacy (we kept ids and shapes).

Attached: error_log_20261119.txt, finlytics-request-sample.json

Error summary (from our side):
- Time window: 2026-11-19T02:10:12Z to 2026-11-19T02:43:08Z
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/rerank
- Response code: 500 / 502 / 504 (mixed)
- Client: finlytics-backend-prod (K8s)
- Batch size: 200 embeddings per request
- Payload size: ~1.2MB compressed per request

We reproduced locally by re-running the same job and saw similar 5xx spikes. Happy to join debugging session.

—Sara
Sara Hunt
Senior Engineering Manager, Integrations | FinLytics
sara.hunt@finlytics.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@finlytics.com>, Joe Alvarez <joe.alvarez@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 19:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call recap and 5xx repro/debugging

Hi Sara — thanks for the logs and payload. I pulled the attached error traces (thanks for including timestamps). Initial observations from our runtime traces:

- We see a burst pattern correlated with high memory usage on the worker handling large batch requests. The runtime reports multiple internal retries which can cascade into 502/504 when timeouts are hit.
- There are a handful of stack traces that point at our tokenization layer hitting an unexpected token length in one item — it caused a per-request exception that surfaced as 500.

Quick actions to try (we can do these live in the debug session):
1) Lower your batch size to 32 or 64 and retry (this reduces per-request memory and KV-cache pressure).
2) Increase your client timeout to 60s for the reranker endpoint.
3) If you can, enable streaming for long rerank responses so partial results return earlier.
4) Send any items that include very long text (>20k chars) separately — that’s what triggered the tokenization exception in our trace.

I’ll attempt to reproduce locally using your sample payload (saved as finlytics-request-sample.json). If I can reproduce, I’ll attach a minimal repro and a patch to our runtime config that avoids the tokenization exception.

Example curl (replace API_KEY):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer API_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d @finlytics-request-sample.json 
  --max-time 60

Stand by — I’ll post updates here.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 21:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call recap and 5xx repro/debugging

Adding a couple ML infra notes while Camila runs the repro: 

- Embedding/reranker patterns: when a single request includes both large embedding arrays and heavy reranking (cross-attention) work, we see memory + kernel-scheduling contention that increases likelihood of 5xx under load. Splitting work across two requests (embed -> store -> rerank with IDs) helps.
- Recommend these immediate changes: use embedding batch size 32, set reranker concurrency to 4 per process, and enable async retries (idempotent) at the client level.

Example of a trimmed request pattern that we recommend (send smaller embedding arrays, then a separate rerank request referencing embedding ids):
{
  "step": "embed",
  "items": ["..."],
  "batch_size": 32
}
{
  "step": "rerank",
  "embedding_ids": ["id_123"],
  "query": "..."
}

If Camila can reproduce the tokenization exception, we’ll push a runtime guard to return a 413-like error for too-large items rather than an internal 500. That should make client-side handling and retries cleaner.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
ML Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@finlytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinLytics integration: post-call recap and 5xx repro/debugging

Thanks team — we tried the smaller batch size (32) and bumping the timeout to 60s and the 5xx rate dropped to near-zero in our re-run (ran over the same 10k items). Camila — we didn’t hit the tokenization exception in this run, so it may have been a single problematic document; we’ll search our corpus and sanitize any very long items (>20k chars).

Next steps from FinLytics:
- We’ll run a full production smoke tomorrow with the new config and report metrics.
- If smoke is successful, I’ll proceed with PO paperwork (we have an internal approvals meeting Monday).

We also uploaded the full Redwood trace bundle you asked for (redwood-traces-20261119.zip) to the drive link in the HubSpot deal.

If you want to close the loop, I can mark this as resolved and we’ll re-open if anything else crops up. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

—Sara
